Consult Summary:
- 19-year-old female presented with 3 days of dysuria and intermittent lower abdominal cramping.
- No fever, flank/back pain, nausea, or vomiting. Clinician impression: uncomplicated urinary tract infection; empiric antibiotics prescribed with safety-net advice.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Dysuria with lower abdominal cramping, onset a few days ago; stinging pain on urination and occasional suprapubic crampy discomfort.
- Associated symptoms: malodorous urine; one episode of visible blood in urine earlier today.
- Pertinent negatives: no urinary frequency noted, no flank/back pain, no fever, no nausea/vomiting, no diarrhea, no vaginal discharge.
- Sexual history pertinent to presentation: sexually active with new boyfriend x ~2 months; uses condoms; last menstrual period “a couple of weeks ago” (doctor restated “three weeks ago”—conflict noted). Patient does not think she is pregnant.
- Clinical impression: acute uncomplicated cystitis/UTI.
- Management discussed: start antibiotics (nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim) for 3 days; increase fluid intake; cranberry juice may help symptomatically; avoid sexual activity until symptoms resolve; continue barrier contraception; safety-net for red flags (fever, back pain, systemic unwellness).

Issue 2:
- Sexual health/contraception context.
- Sexually active; uses condoms consistently.
- No prior STI screen reported.
- Advised to continue barrier contraception and avoid sex during symptomatic period.
- Advised to consider a pregnancy test if concerned.

Issue 3:
- Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) history.
- Currently asymptomatic; bowel movements reported as normal; no diarrhea.

Medications:
- Planned: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim — one tablet twice daily for 3 days; specific agent not documented; dose/route not documented.
- Over-the-counter bicarbonate taken recently for symptoms — dose/route/frequency not documented; not effective.
- No regular prescription medications reported.

Allergies:
- Clindamycin — causes swelling.

Past Medical History:
- Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).

Social History:
- Lives in an apartment near college with friends.
- Student (biology).
- Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: drinks socially on weekends.

Preventative History:
- STI screen: never done.
- Other preventive care (cervical screening, mammogram, prostate test, fecal occult blood test, bone density, vaccinations, optometry, skin check): not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: not documented.
- Examination findings: not documented (clinician stated they would proceed to exam; no findings recorded).

Plan:
- Start empiric antibiotic course: nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim, 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days (agent/dose/route not documented).
- Increase oral fluids; cranberry juice may help symptoms.
- Avoid sexual activity until symptoms resolve; continue condom use.
- Safety-net: seek care if fever, flank/back pain, or feeling more unwell develop (concern for possible ascending infection).
- Follow-up: if symptoms not improved by end of the week, call or return for reassessment.
- Pregnancy: if concerned, perform a pregnancy test.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: vitals, physical exam findings, urinalysis/urine culture, pregnancy test result, STI screening, specific antibiotic agent and dose/route documented, comprehensive medication reconciliation.
- Internal conflicts: last menstrual period documented as “a couple of weeks ago,” while clinician restated “three weeks ago” (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: generally clear with minor brief audio/clarity gaps; no impact on key clinical details.
